# HarnessDock v0.1.5

HarnessDock `v0.1.5` is the formal stable publication built on the validated `v0.1.5-rc.2` candidate line. The client version is stable `0.1.5`; the sealed desktop Runtime remains pinned to DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2` at commit `fb2c4b9e698e30edb738bca4cf0618587db7d203` so Runtime provenance stays exact and reproducible.

This release is published as a normal GitHub Release (`draft=false`, `prerelease=false`) and is immutable after publication. Every asset must come from the same exact `main` SHA and pass the full candidate, same-SHA CI, installed Windows startup, Runtime identity and checksum gates.

## Runtime alignment

- Pinned upstream source: `dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2`.
- Pinned upstream commit: `fb2c4b9e698e30edb738bca4cf0618587db7d203`.
- Windows, Linux and macOS package the official upstream source closure as a sealed local Runtime.
- Android and iOS remain Remote Gateway clients and do not embed a desktop Runtime.
- Runtime `imageIdentity`, generation nonce, managed PID and exact local origin remain authoritative.

## dsh profile startup

Diagnostics exposes validated Runtime launch preferences without allowing arbitrary executable replacement:

- **Profile** maps to `dsh --profile <name>`; default remains `web`.
- **DSH_HOME** is an optional absolute profile/config root.
- **Auto** starts the selected profile first; `web` keeps plugin isolation/recovery while non-web failures fall back to Safe web startup.
- **Direct** performs one selected-profile attempt and preserves the first error.
- **Safe** always uses built-in `web` with a private temporary `DSH_HOME`.

Launch settings are resolved once per Runtime generation. Editing settings cannot hot-mutate an in-flight `RuntimeLease`, and launch-settings IPC is available only to the local Diagnostics WebView.

## Startup, refresh and lifecycle

- Startup proceeds toward Harness Web immediately after Host Kernel setup; optional tray/updater/menu initialization does not serially block the primary Web path.
- The startup splash and primary Harness WebView use explicit first-paint backgrounds to avoid default white frames while content is still painting.
- Refresh, Runtime restart, Safe Mode restart and normal quit use an in-place lifecycle overlay after Harness Web is visible.
- Concurrent lifecycle operations are rejected while Harness navigation is already loading, preventing overlapping watchdogs and Runtime churn.
- A corrupted launch-preferences file fails open to `web + Auto` rather than replacing the primary Harness Web path with a settings error.

## Managed-process shutdown hardening

- Windows managed Runtime descendants remain inside `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` Job Objects.
- Unix managed children remain isolated in dedicated process groups.
- Shutdown closes new-process admission first, performs strict process-tree cleanup, observes actor/registry drain, then performs a final idempotent no-orphan pass.
- The Windows installed-client gate proves bundled `node.exe` is actually running, closes HarnessDock normally, and requires HarnessDock, Runtime and bundled Node processes from the installed tree to reach zero.
- Navigation watchdogs and Host Kernel replies use nonblocking Tokio primitives.

## Compatibility and safety

- Profile names use upstream single-component validation and cannot traverse outside `$DSH_HOME/profiles`.
- Explicit `DSH_HOME` values must be absolute paths.
- Plugin quarantine schema v3 is scoped by dsh base version, selected profile and effective `DSH_HOME`; legacy unscoped records are invalidated rather than reused across a different plugin tree.
- Remote Harness Web does not receive high-privilege Tauri IPC.
- The desktop WebView Runtime ACL remains bound to the exact managed `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` lease origin instead of broad localhost access.
- The release keeps Tauri-only product boundaries and does not reintroduce Electron compatibility hosts.

## Release assets and verification

The stable release contract contains exactly 15 assets covering Windows NSIS, Linux AppImage/DEB, macOS x64/arm64 packages, Android APK/AAB, iOS simulator package, four deterministic sealed Runtime archives, and `SHA256SUMS`.

Publication is allowed only after the exact same `main` SHA has a successful `tauri-candidate`, ordinary CI, and installed Windows packaged-startup gate. Release assembly then recomputes Runtime identity after artifact handoff, verifies the exact asset set and SHA-256 payloads, and only then writes the immutable GitHub Release.

## Upstream package note

The bundled Runtime is sourced from the immutable upstream Git tag/commit above. If the umbrella `@deepseek-ai/dsh` npm publication lags that Git tag, HarnessDock does not invent a nonexistent npm tarball or integrity value; the official source closure remains the release provenance source of truth.
